m.s: A Sunday arvo job. Cut {beef_chuck} into big 5cm chunks, pat dry with paper towel and season well. Heat a drizzle of oil in a large heavy pot over high heat. Brown the beef in batches for 3 to 4 minutes a side until a deep crust forms. Crowd the pot and it steams instead, so keep the batches small. Set aside on a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium. Finely dice {onion} and {carrot}, add to the pot and cook for 10 minutes, scraping up the brown bits, until soft and sweet. Add {garlic}, crushed, and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in {tompaste} and cook for 2 minutes until it darkens to brick red. Add {tintom}, {oregano} and {stockpowder}, then return the beef and its juices. Pour in just enough water to cover the beef.

Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 3 hours (or in a 160°C oven) until the beef falls apart when pushed with a spoon. Stir every 45 minutes and add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Shred the beef in the pot with two forks. Simmer with the lid off for 15 minutes until thick and glossy. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Cook {pasta} in a big pot of well-salted boiling water until al dente. Scoop out a mug of the pasta water, then drain. Toss the pasta through the ragu with a splash of that water so it coats every piece. Serve with grated {parm} and chopped {parsley}.

l: Keep a little pasta water to loosen it when reheating. It honestly eats better the next day. Keeps 4 days in the fridge, and the ragu freezes well.
g: GF pasta in a separate pot with its own spoon, sauced from the main pot before the regular pasta goes in. Check the stock powder.
